_note: The first-person arms from KINEMATION's FPS Animation Ultimate (docs/PLAN_FIRST_PERSON_ARMS.md), a paid pack: its files are made by `npm run paid` (tools/import-fparms.ts) into models/paid/arms/, never in git, shipped only with the game server. `general` are the clips every gun shares; `packGuns` are the pack's guns whose holds we use, each with its arms clips (A_FP_) and its gun's own clips (A_W_, which move the pack gun's magazine, bolt and charging handle), and the pack gun's model, read for its measurements and drawn only by the tools; `guns` maps our guns to them. The owner's order (2026-09-27): USSO and BOOG first, made right and shipped, then the rest. Ours: which pack gun stands in for which of ours is chosen on pictures at the owner's view.

MPS5._hold: Fitted by tools/pack-fit.ts, then joint by joint by tools/pack-solve.ts joints and tools/pack-thumb.ts, 2026-09-28. The fit alone left the right hand's seen skin up to 8 mm into the grip and its thumb 12 mm in, lying over the receiver where no small turn moved it; now no seen skin is more than 4 mm in, held, pointing, racking, aimed, swapping or picking up (tools/e2e.ts pack frames; tools/pack-frames.ts flags no frame of the reload, swap, aim or pickup).
MPS5._solve: tools/pack-solve.ts wrists, 2026-09-28: the shoulders and the pointing arm where the wrists are straightest, the arms no more in the picture (13.8% of their skin then 14.1%). Wrists left and right 38 and 20 degrees at rest, 44 and 21 aimed; pointing 50 (68 before), the tip on its spot; 39 early in a swap (tools/e2e.ts pack frames).

L96X._hold: Fitted by tools/pack-fit.ts, then joint by joint by tools/pack-solve.ts joints and tools/pack-thumb.ts (the right thumb and middle finger), 2026-09-28. The left hand then moved off the magazine onto the fore-end (the owner, 2026-09-28: "for the boog, the support hand is holding the mag"): BOOG's magazine is further ahead of its trigger than the L96X's, and the pack's hold put the palm's middle 10.4 cm back from its front (fprig.ts palmAhead). Moved 14 cm ahead the pack's grip, made for a thicker fore-end, lay flat against BOOG's side with its fingers 5 to 10 cm off it, so tools/pack-grip.ts searched the hand's move and turn for a grip there: the palm on the gun 2.7 cm ahead of the magazine, the index, middle and little fingers and the thumb on it (the ring finger 4 cm off it: a search of its joints over their whole range found no turn onto it short of a contorted finger), none of it in the gun, the wrist 18 degrees.
L96X._solve: tools/pack-solve.ts wrists, 2026-09-28, with the left hand on the fore-end: the shoulders where the wrists are straightest with the arm reaching it (the pack's own shoulders left it 1.7 cm and more short past 6 cm ahead), and the pointing arm. Wrists left and right 12 and 20 degrees at rest, 46 and 23 aimed, pointing 49. The left arm now reaches along the gun into the picture (36% of the arms' skin in it at rest, none before), as a rifleman's does with the hand out on the fore-end. The left shoulder then 4 cm further forward than that search put it: at rest the arm was straight, at all of its reach, and the bolt worked after a shot pushes the gun 5 cm ahead, which left it 1.9 cm short and the hand back on the magazine.

_camera: Where the pack's camera sits in its rig, metres, the rig facing +z: its FPSPlayer prefab's Camera (field of view 80, near 0.01) at 0.012, 1.654, 0.06, 9 cm over the head bone. fprig.ts puts it on our eye, so the arms' shoulders stay where the pack made them, just out of the picture; the gun goes where our view puts it and both hands reach it (KINEMATION's own rig: the gun on its weapon bone, the hands on it by IK). Hung off our gun instead, the arms' shoulders and sleeves came into the view and filled a third of it.
_adsShoulder: Metres both shoulders go back in the sights, on top of the pack gun's own clavicle offset (its settings asset): our sights bring the gun to the eye nearer than KINEMATION's player does (it stops short by the gun's aim point offset, 10 to 12 cm), and with the shoulder where the hold put it the USSO's right wrist bent 109 degrees aimed and its left 70 (tools/e2e.ts, the pack's wristBend).
_hipPitch: The barrel's pitch at rest with these arms, radians up: level, as the view's own arms held the same gun before them (measured: 0.3 degrees on the USSO, -0.1 on BOOG). The fit tilts our gun up about its trigger to meet the pack's left palm, 10 degrees on the USSO and 12 on BOOG (measured), and the muzzle pointed up and to the left standing still; the owner, 2026-09-28: "look at hyperscape and apex, in the chilling / standing position, the gun is never like that", and again at 2 degrees, drawn at the pack camera's field of view (80, where ours is 92 at the default setting): "I STILL FEEL like the guns when resting are still too angled up and to the left too much, like the view angle isn't how it was originally". The view takes the tilt back off down to this, the hands following the gun (viewmodel.ts), and keeps every gun's 3 degrees in toward the crosshair; the gun camera's field of view is the game's own, as before these arms.
_sprint: The pack's sprint on the gun (fprig.ts locomotion): its swing, 51 degrees across the body, comes in over `easeIn` s while sprinting and goes over `easeOut` s the moment you fire, aim or reload, and comes back `fireHold` s after the last shot. SpeedKills sprints whenever you move forward, firing included, and with the sprint on by speed alone the owner fired from a gun swung across the body, the tracers nowhere near the crosshair (2026-09-27, the live server). In the sights none of the pack's walk or sprint is kept. `swing` is how much of the pack's sprint (its tactical carry, the gun swung across the chest and rolled on its side) is used: none. SpeedKills sprints whenever you move, and with it on the owner saw the gun "crossed and inverted" the whole time he moved (2026-09-27); the run keeps the ready hold, the walk's bob carried on at a run.
_reload: The reload with the bought arms, the owner's (2026-09-27): "point a finger at it while it phases out and in for a reload and then smack the charging handle ... same with the sniper ... a nice combo of the two". Shares of the reload: the left hand leaves the gun over `point` and points at the magazine, its index finger out and its tip `gap` m off the magazine's left face, the hand `reach` m back from the tip along `aim` (in the gun's frame: right, up, ahead), while the gun turns its underside toward you (gunfeel.json reload.twist); the magazine phases out over `phaseOut` and a new one in over `phaseIn`, staying in the gun, and seats at `seat`; then over `rack` the pack's own hands work the gun: each pack gun's `rack` names the clip and the share of it where they do (measured off its gun clip: the MPS5's empty reload slaps its handle forward at 0.69, the L96X's fire clip works its bolt over 0.30 to 0.48), and the hands go back to the hold. It had been the pack's whole reload, the magazine carried out of the gun to the belt and back, its phase out of sight. `twist` turns the gun while the hand points (radians, and metres before the view's scale), smaller than gunfeel.json's own: at that one the gun filled the middle of the screen and the pointing hand came up to the eye. A pack gun's own `twist` replaces it: the USSO's magazine sits low, and at the shared one its pointing hand was below the screen's edge. Which face of the magazine the finger comes at is `face` (in the gun's frame; -1 on x its left face, -1 on y its bottom), `aim` the way it points, and a pack gun's own `point` replaces the three: the BOOG's magazine is a thin plate low on the gun's left side, and pointed at from its left the hand sat between the eye and it (2026-09-27, a picture with the magazine tinted red), so its finger comes up at its bottom, the gun pitched and rolled more to show it. The pointing arm's elbow bends toward `elbow` from its shoulder (in the view: right, up, toward you), hanging down: bent the way the hold had it, the USSO's point, 22 cm from the shoulder, folded the arm so tight that on the way its elbow passed 9 cm in front of the eye and the sleeve filled the view for a tenth of the reload (measured bone by bone, 2026-09-27). The magazine slides as it phases (the owner, 2026-09-28: "drop out and pixelate, and then pixelate and slide in with a distance from start to end"): the old one `slide` view metres down its own length as it goes, the new one from there up into the gun as it comes (the USSO's is 17 cm long, BOOG's 12 cm tall, measured in the view), and the finger follows it. The fingertip is `shift` view metres left and down of the point it points at (the owner: "down and left more on both, not by too much"), the hand turned `aimAt` of the way from its forearm's line to point at it. From the point the gun goes straight into its rack pose (a pack gun's rack `pose`, view radians and metres) over `rackBlend` of the reload, and a pack gun's rack `gunKeep` is the share of its rack clip's own gun motion kept: the MPS5's empty reload is made for a handle at the front of its gun, and the USSO's is at the back, 35 cm from the eye, so carried over the left hand came to 27 cm and filled a third of the view, the gun thrown small and far to the middle (2026-09-28, every frame of it measured and looked at; tools/pack-frames.ts). The hand points along the line from its shoulder to the fingertip, `bend` of the way toward `aim` (along `aim` alone the wrist bent 107 to 126 degrees), at `at` of the magazine's height from its bottom (its middle, up a pistol grip, is hidden by the other hand). A pack gun's rack `shift` moves a hand while its rack clip works the gun, view metres along our gun's axes: the L96X's right hand throws its bolt where BOOG's body is, the glove 15 mm into it; 21 mm out along the gun's width leaves none of it through the gun where it is seen over the bolt's throw (searched, 2026-09-28, with the hold fitted joint by joint). A pack gun's rack `grab` closes the left hand on our handle itself: the owner, 2026-09-28, "we get close to it, but our fingers don't grip it, it's like 80% of the way there". The USSO's handle is a knob standing a centimetre off the gun's left side, which no closed hand holds without going into the gun (10 mm and more, every roll of the pack's own grip and every turn of a hand closed round it, searched), so it is a `pinch`: the thumb and forefinger's tips (`hook` off the knob, in our gun's frame) on it, the other three fingers curled into the palm, the hand turned with its knuckles `along` and its palm facing `palm` in our gun's frame, and the forefinger `curl` (below 0, opened) from the pack's grip. Searched by what of the hand is through the gun where it is seen, its gap to the gun and its wrist: none through, touching, the wrist 22 degrees. `clear`: metres the left hand bows out past the gun's left side on its way to the point and back, the most a third of the way from the hold (6.75 x share x (1 - share)^2), where the magazine is in the way, and next to none as the finger lands: BOOG's hand, on the fore-end ahead of the magazine, went 15 mm through the magazine going straight, and bowed evenly the finger landed 50 to 74 degrees off its spot.
_swap: On a swap or holster the arms drop out of the picture as the gun phases out, and come back up to take the next one as it phases in (the owner: "the guns fly in and out but the arms stay in a weird position"): at the phase's bottom the whole rig is `drop` m lower, `back` m nearer and pitched `pitch` radians down, about the eye. With `clips` of the pack's own swap on top (fprig.ts swapMotion, its Rifle_Unequip and Rifle_Equip, measured: the gun swung 29 cm across, 34 cm in to the chest and turned 58 degrees, the hands on it all the way), the one into the other over `cross` of the swap either side of its middle, where the guns change; the owner, 2026-09-28: "look for more things we can do with it, especially when we swap guns, what the hands and arms can do". The arms drop only from `dropFrom` of the way out of the picture (the gun all but gone): from the start they left the gun flying on its own while the pack's swap carried it.
_pickup: Taking something off the ground (main.ts applyLoot, any item but a gun, which comes into the hands by the swap): the pack's pickup clip, its left hand down and back up, over `seconds` (the clip's own length), eased in and out over `ease` of it. `gunKeep` is the share of the clip's own motion of the gun kept: all of it tipped the gun up onto its side and bent the right wrist to 88 degrees.
_free: The bought arms off a gun (fprig.ts free, handTurn; the owner, 2026-09-28: the fists were "the old fists and not our new bought arms"). `fist`: each finger joint's bend in a fist, radians, along the axis the pack's own grip bends it (its first gun's pose clip, the right hand round a pistol grip). `thumb`: each fist's thumb joints turned on top of that, radians about each joint's own axes, searched by tools/fist-thumb.ts to lie across the index and middle fingers' middle bones with none of it in them: bent as the grip bends it, its tip stood 1.3 to 1.6 of a phalanx out ahead of the fist like a pointing finger, now 0.42 (left) and 0.14 (right). `palmSign`: which way off the knuckles each hand's palm faces, opposite on the two hands, which are mirror images (the right at -1 like the left faced its palm out and up, the hand rolled 159 degrees on its forearm and the glove's cuff split from the sleeve; the owner, 2026-09-28: "the right arm is clearly still so fucked up ... just put the guns away and look at the right arm"). `palm`: on an inspect, the open left hand's knuckles and the way its palm faces, in the view's space (x right, y up, z back toward the eye), with the hack floating over it. `pull`: the fists moved from the view's own fists' place toward the eye, view metres (in, up, back): the bought arms are shorter than the view's, and there they were straight out, 97% of their reach. `twistShare`: of a hand's roll on its forearm, the share its twist bone halfway down the forearm takes, where the hand is posed here rather than by a clip (the fists, the open palm): with none, the whole roll was at the wrist, and the open palm's 150 degrees split the glove's cuff from the sleeve.
_inspectPalm: Where the open left hand's wrist is on an inspect, view metres (x right, y up, z back toward the eye): 3 cm left of and 12 cm over where it first was, searched by tools/palm-place.ts on both guns for no hack card over the gun at any moment of the inspect (the owner, 2026-09-28: "held higher and slightly more to the left so it doesn't bug in and out with the gun"; there, 34 to 87% of a card was over it), the arm reaching and the wrist straight enough; and how the hack floats over the palm: `bob` metres up and down at `rate` a second, `spin` radians side to side. `lift`: how far off the palm the hack floats, view metres (at 6 cm it sat in the palm). `pair`: with two hacks carried, each has its card, `gap` metres apart across the view and at `scale` of one card's size, side by side over the palm. `clear`: metres the hand bows out past the gun's left side on its way up to the palm and back, the most near the gun (6.75 x share x (1 - share)^2): straight, it went 9 to 25 mm through the gun. The cards come up only once the hand is halfway there.
_guns: Which pack gun stands in for which of ours, chosen on pictures at the owner's view: the USSO's is the MPS5, a compact SMG held by its handguard, its charging handle worked from empty; the Striker-V, the first tried, holds its long magazine as a grip, 22 cm under where the USSO's short one sits, and the hand could not be on both. BOOG's is the L96X, a bolt sniper that works its bolt after every shot. A pack gun's gun clips list only those the import makes a file of: the MPS5's and the L96X's A_W pose are stills with no animation, which tools/import-fparms.ts writes nothing for, and asked for they were a 404 on every page once the arms load at the start for the fists (the live check caught it, 2026-09-28); the rig runs without them. A pack gun's `hold` is each hand's fit onto our grip (fprig.ts HandFit: `shift`, `rot`, `open`, `turn`, `joint`), measured into place by tools/pack-fit.ts, then joint by joint by tools/pack-solve.ts and tools/pack-thumb.ts until no seen skin is more than 4 mm into the gun anywhere in its moves. Its `shoulders` move the clavicles on top of the pack's own offsets, metres in the rig, at rest (`l`, `r`) and aimed (`adsL`, `adsR`), to where the wrists are straightest without more of the arms in the picture (tools/pack-solve.ts wrists). Its `point` can carry its own `elbow`, `reach` and `aimAt` for the reload's pointing arm (the reload's otherwise), searched the same way with the fingertip kept on its spot.
_inspectPack: An inspect in the bought arms' hands (viewmodel.ts): the forearm turns the gun, rolled about the right forearm's own line through the grip (measured off the rig at rest) by `roll[0]` radians to show its left side over `show` of the inspect, over to `roll[1]` the other way over `turn` to show its right, and back over `settle`, lifted `lift` metres; the right forearm takes the roll along its length (fprig.ts spreadTwist). Turned about the gun's own axes, the view's own inspect bent the right wrist to 99 degrees, and about a long gun's middle BOOG's grip swung 20 cm out of the arm's reach. Settled before the open left hand comes back to the gun (inspectPalm ease): settling as it came, BOOG's body swung through the hand. `flourish`: a new gun's first draw in these hands, radians the forearm rolls the gun out and back the same way (sin over the flourish), in place of the view's whole twirl round the barrel, which in a hand on the grip wrung the wrist 152 degrees and put the hand through the gun. The left hand stays on the gun through it: at 0.9 its wrist bent 70 degrees, at 0.5 62, so 0.42.
